---
title: "About me"
---

I'm Riccardo. I studied finance at Tor Vergata in Rome, did a stint at ING in Milan, a summer at
Baird in New York, and some advisory work between Palermo and Milan. Most recently I spent a year
on financial management and budgetary reporting at an EU agency in Amsterdam.

What I actually do is narrower than any of that sounds. Behind almost every number an organisation
reports there is a person exporting a file and filtering it by hand. I find those people, work out
what they are really doing, and build the thing that does it for them. Then I write it all down,
because a tool nobody can run after I leave is not a tool, it is a liability with a nice icon.

## Three things I believe about this work

```{=html}
<div class="principles">
  <div class="p-card"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <h4>Agree the definitions first</h4>
    <p>The model is the easy part. Getting two departments to accept one definition of a field is the
      part that decides whether the thing survives contact with a real month end.</p></div>
  <div class="p-card"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <h4>Make the right action the easy one</h4>
    <p>A tool is worth exactly what it gets used. That usually means fewer options rather than more,
      and making the wrong move hard to do by accident.</p></div>
  <div class="p-card"><span class="mark" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <h4>Write it down or it does not exist</h4>
    <p>Everything ships with rendered documentation and a guide. Partly for the team. Mostly because
      I will forget how it works within about six weeks.</p></div>
</div>
```

## My competitive record

Since you clicked: I was the **rank one builder in the world La Canea**, entered into the Grepolis
Hall of Fame. It is a browser strategy game from 2011. I know that is a genuinely ridiculous thing
to still be pleased about this many years later.

However, I am pleased about it [ANYWAYS]{.anyway}.

I also play **BTDB2**, a monkey game about popping balloons, well enough to have taken a World
Champion title and played the World Masters Tournament. In a world of admittedly modest size: just
twenty-four players.

Neither of these is useful in any way, shape or form. Both come from the same instinct: hone the
thing until it is as good as I can get it, grind slowly up, and reach the peak.
